You are helping a researcher prepare for an upcoming academic conference on Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). The conference is called "RLHF Summit 2026" and will take place on April 10, 2026 from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM at the San Francisco Convention Center.

First, search the academic paper databases for papers related to "reinforcement learning from human feedback". You should find at least 5 relevant papers. Exclude any papers that are not directly about RLHF or human feedback in the context of language model training (for example, papers about self-play in board games should be excluded).

For each of the relevant RLHF papers you find, retrieve the full manuscript source to examine their methodology sections in detail. Pay attention to the key techniques each paper introduces.

Next, create a PowerPoint presentation called RLHF_Conference_Report.pptx in your workspace. The presentation should include the following slides:

First, a title slide with the title "RLHF Summit 2026 Conference Preparation Report" and subtitle "Key Papers in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback".

First, an overview slide that introduces the field of RLHF and why it matters for language model alignment.

First, one slide for each of the relevant papers (at least 5 slides). Each paper slide should include the paper title, the authors, and a brief summary of the key contribution and methodology. Make sure to include papers about instruction following with human feedback, learning to summarize from human feedback, constitutional AI, direct preference optimization, and proximal policy optimization.

First, a summary slide that synthesizes the key themes across all papers.

After creating the presentation, create a calendar event for the RLHF Summit 2026 conference. The event should be on April 10, 2026 from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with the location set to "San Francisco Convention Center" and a description that mentions this is a conference about reinforcement learning from human feedback.

Finally, send an email to your collaborators at collaborators@rlhf-lab.org with the subject "RLHF Summit 2026 Preparation Materials". The email body should briefly describe that you have prepared a conference report covering key RLHF papers and created a calendar event for the conference. Mention the date (April 10, 2026) and location in the email.

If you are working in a multi-agent setup, designate exactly one agent to create and write RLHF_Conference_Report.pptx, and have the other agents coordinate with it — do not have multiple agents write to the same file, as concurrent writers can overwrite each other.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

Before Wave 1, the main agent must freeze exactly five required paper slots—InstructGPT, learning to summarize from human feedback, Constitutional AI, DPO, and PPO—and the conference, presentation, calendar, and email contract. It must assign one stable paper identity per slot and exclude unrelated human-feedback or self-play work. Resolve the task-visible workspace directory from the runtime allowed-directory listing (or the literal accessible-workspace directory already supplied by the harness), freeze `<workspace_root>`, and reject bare `/workspace` and dumps/run-specific paths. Because the conference event is fixed and independent of paper research, the main agent must search for the exact event before dispatch and, in the same orchestration response that launches Wave 1, create at most the one missing event for 2026-04-10 from 09:00 to 17:00 at `San Francisco Convention Center`; preserve the calendar tool's default timezone, use no attendees, and retain the event ID for later read-back. Do not retry creation after an ambiguous failure.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 5 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to research instruction following with human feedback.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Use one explore sub-agent to research learning to summarize from human feedback.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Use one explore sub-agent to research Constitutional AI.
   4. explore 3 (academic-literature-researcher 3): Use one explore sub-agent to research Direct Preference Optimization.
   5. explore 4 (academic-literature-researcher 4): Use one explore sub-agent to research Proximal Policy Optimization.

Each Wave 1 sub-agent must search the granted academic sources read-only for only its assigned slot, validate title/abstract relevance, retrieve the full available manuscript/source, and return a compact source-backed record with authors, contribution, methodology, stable ID/title, source/section coverage, and missing-field status. Explore is read-only, so do not write files or create slides, calendar events, or email.

After Wave 1, the main agent must reconcile the five stable IDs and distinguish PPO's foundational algorithm role from direct language-model alignment evidence; it must freeze one literal canonical five-paper packet and reject invented claims. The deck and final email consume exactly this packet without re-researching or rephrasing factual fields.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 1 sub-agent for the following numbered sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own `<workspace_root>/RLHF_Conference_Report.pptx` exclusively. To avoid a long sequence of slide-by-slide calls, use one `python_execute` with the installed `python-pptx` package to create the complete deck atomically from the canonical packet: required title and overview slides, exactly one substantive slide for each of the five frozen papers, and a final synthesis slide. Then use the presentation read tools once to verify slide count, titles, five-paper coverage, and source-backed authors/methods. Return path and validation; do not create calendar or email state.

After Wave 2, the main agent must verify the deck and read back the retained calendar event, requiring exactly one matching RLHF Summit 2026 event on 2026-04-10 from 09:00 to 17:00 at the specified location. It must then search sent mail and send at most one missing email to collaborators@rlhf-lab.org with the exact subject and verified report/event details. Perform final deck, event, and message checks before completion.

nodes.text:
You are gathering scholarly evidence for a conference preparation report on Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) for language model alignment.

TASK:
1. Search arXiv (use the search-arxiv tool with keywords like "reinforcement learning from human feedback", "instruction following human feedback", "direct preference optimization", "constitutional AI", "learning to summarize human feedback", "proximal policy optimization") to identify relevant papers.
2. Select AT LEAST 5 papers that are DIRECTLY about RLHF / human feedback for language model training. Exclude papers not about RLHF for LMs (e.g., self-play in board games like AlphaGo must be excluded).
3. The final set MUST cover these 5 topics (one paper each):
   a. Instruction following with human feedback (expected: "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback" / InstructGPT, arXiv 2203.02155)
   b. Learning to summarize from human feedback (expected: arXiv 2009.01325)
   c. Constitutional AI (expected: "Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback", arXiv 2212.08073)
   d. Direct Preference Optimization (expected: arXiv 2305.18290)
   e. Proximal Policy Optimization (expected: "Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms", arXiv 1707.06347)
   You may add a 6th relevant RLHF paper if you find a good one, but 5 is sufficient.
4. For EACH selected paper: retrieve the abstract (get_paper_abstract) AND use list_paper_sections + get_paper_section to read the methodology/method/approach sections in detail.

DELIVERABLE — return a structured report with, for each paper:
- arXiv ID
- Exact paper title
- Full author list (or first 3-5 authors + "et al." if very long)
- Key contribution (2-3 sentences)
- Methodology summary (4-6 sentences covering the key techniques: e.g., reward model training, PPO setup, preference data collection, the DPO closed-form loss, constitutional AI's two-stage SL/RL process, etc.)
- One-sentence confirmation of why it is directly about RLHF for language models.

Be precise and factual — this will be used verbatim-ish in a conference presentation. Do not write any files; just return the report.
Research key RLHF papers

You are the SOLE agent authorized to create the file RLHF_Conference_Report.pptx. No other agent will touch it.

GOAL: Create a PowerPoint presentation at this exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Kimi-K3/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-conference-prep/workspace/RLHF_Conference_Report.pptx

Use the pptx MCP tools (create_presentation, add_slide, manage_text / populate_placeholder / add_bullet_points, save_presentation). Build a clean, professional deck (business/modern style, readable font sizes, no overflowing text). The deck must contain exactly these 8 slides:

SLIDE 1 — Title slide:
- Title: "RLHF Summit 2026 Conference Preparation Report"
- Subtitle: "Key Papers in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback"
- (Optional small line: "April 10, 2026 · San Francisco Convention Center")

SLIDE 2 — Overview slide, title "Overview: RLHF and Language Model Alignment":
Bullet content (you may lightly polish wording but keep the substance):
- RLHF = Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: aligning language models with human preferences and intent
- Pretraining and supervised fine-tuning alone leave models misaligned: unhelpful, untruthful, or toxic outputs
- Core RLHF recipe: collect human preference comparisons → train a reward model → optimize the LM policy with RL (typically PPO) under a KL constraint
- RLHF powers modern assistants (InstructGPT/ChatGPT-style systems); variants like RLAIF and DPO reduce cost and complexity
- This report reviews 5 foundational papers spanning the full RLHF stack

SLIDES 3–7 — One slide per paper below. Each slide must include the paper title (as slide title or first line), the authors, arXiv ID, key contribution, and methodology summary. Keep bullets concise.

Paper 1 (slide title e.g. "Instruction Following with Human Feedback (InstructGPT)"):
- Title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
- Authors: Long Ouyang, Jeff Wu, Xu Jiang, Diogo Almeida, Carroll Wainwright, Pamela Mishkin, et al. (OpenAI) — arXiv:2203.02155, NeurIPS 2022
- Key contribution: The canonical InstructGPT paper; established the standard 3-stage RLHF pipeline (SFT → reward model → PPO). A 1.3B InstructGPT is preferred by labelers to 175B GPT-3, with better truthfulness and lower toxicity.
- Methodology: (1) SFT on labeler-written demonstrations; (2) reward model trained on human rankings of model outputs; (3) PPO fine-tuning against the RM with a KL-divergence penalty to the SFT model.

Paper 2 (slide title e.g. "Learning to Summarize from Human Feedback"):
- Title: Learning to summarize from human feedback
- Authors: Nisan Stiennon, Long Ouyang, Jeff Wu, Daniel Ziegler, Ryan Lowe, Chelsea Voss, Alec Radford, Dario Amodei, Paul Christiano (OpenAI) — arXiv:2009.01325, NeurIPS 2020
- Key contribution: Early rigorous demonstration that LMs can directly optimize human preferences instead of proxy metrics, applied to Reddit TL;DR abstractive summarization; summaries preferred over much larger supervised models.
- Methodology: Reward model trained on human pairwise summary comparisons; frozen RM used as reward for PPO fine-tuning of the summarization policy; KL regularization to the supervised baseline limits reward hacking; RM iteratively retrained on on-policy samples.

Paper 3 (slide title e.g. "Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback"):
- Title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
- Authors: Yuntao Bai, Saurav Kadavath, Sandipan Kundu, Amanda Askell, Jackson Kernion, et al. (Anthropic) — arXiv:2212.08073
- Key contribution: Trains a harmless assistant guided by a short written "constitution" of principles; AI-generated feedback (RLAIF) largely replaces human harmlessness labels while staying helpful and non-evasive.
- Methodology: Phase 1 (supervised): model critiques and revises its own responses per constitutional principles, then is fine-tuned on revisions. Phase 2 (RL/RLAIF): AI generates preference comparisons using the constitution; a preference model trained on these labels provides the reward for RL fine-tuning.

Paper 4 (slide title e.g. "Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)"):
- Title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
- Authors: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma, Eric Mitchell, Stefano Ermon, Christopher D. Manning, Chelsea Finn (Stanford) — arXiv:2305.18290, NeurIPS 2023
- Key contribution: Achieves the RLHF objective (reward maximization under a KL constraint) in a single simple training stage — no explicit reward model, no RL, no sampling during fine-tuning; stable and lightweight.
- Methodology: Uses the closed-form mapping between the optimal KL-constrained policy and the reward function; substituting into the Bradley–Terry preference model yields a binary cross-entropy loss over preference pairs on policy vs. reference log-probability ratios; β controls KL strength; the policy implicitly fits the reward model.

Paper 5 (slide title e.g. "Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO): The RL Engine of RLHF"):
- Title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
- Authors: John Schulman, Filip Wolski, Prafulla Dhariwal, Alec Radford, Oleg Klimov (OpenAI) — arXiv:1707.06347
- Key contribution: Policy-gradient RL family with TRPO-level stability but far simpler, more general, and more sample-efficient; the de facto RL optimizer in RLHF pipelines (used by InstructGPT and the summarization work).
- Methodology: Alternates between sampling rollouts and optimizing a clipped surrogate objective (probability ratio clipped to [1−ε, 1+ε] times advantage) with multiple minibatch epochs; combined objective adds value-function loss and entropy bonus; prevents destructively large policy updates.

SLIDE 8 — Summary slide, title "Summary: Key Themes Across Papers":
Bullets:
- Common pipeline: human (or AI) preference comparisons → scalar reward/preference signal → policy optimization with a KL trust region
- PPO is the workhorse RL optimizer; clipping and KL penalties are essential for stable LM alignment
- Feedback source is evolving: human labels (InstructGPT, summarization) → AI feedback (Constitutional AI/RLAIF) → implicit rewards (DPO)
- Efficiency trend: DPO collapses the 3-stage pipeline into one supervised-style loss, lowering cost and complexity
- Open challenges: reward hacking, scalable oversight, preference data quality, balancing helpfulness vs. harmlessness

REQUIREMENTS:
- Exactly 8 slides, in the order above.
- All paper slides must show: title, authors, arXiv ID, contribution, methodology.
- Text must fit slides (use concise bullets; optimize_slide_text if needed).
- Save to the exact path given above, verify the save succeeded (e.g., get_presentation_info / extract_presentation_text), and report back: the file path, slide count, and a one-line confirmation per slide that its content is present.
Build RLHF conference PPTX

You are handling two external workflow actions for RLHF conference preparation. Complete BOTH.

ACTION 1 — Create a Google Calendar event:
- Summary/title: "RLHF Summit 2026"
- Date: April 10, 2026
- Time: 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM (use ISO format, e.g. 2026-04-10T09:00:00-07:00 to 2026-04-10T17:00:00-07:00, timeZone America/Los_Angeles)
- Location: "San Francisco Convention Center"
- Description: must mention that this is a conference about reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). Suggested: "RLHF Summit 2026 — a full-day academic conference on reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), covering key papers on instruction following, reward modeling, PPO, Constitutional AI, and Direct Preference Optimization."
- After creating, note the event ID returned.

ACTION 2 — Send an email:
- To: collaborators@rlhf-lab.org
- Subject: "RLHF Summit 2026 Preparation Materials"
- Body (plain text): briefly explain that a conference preparation report covering key RLHF papers has been prepared (the PowerPoint file RLHF_Conference_Report.pptx, covering instruction following with human feedback, learning to summarize from human feedback, Constitutional AI, Direct Preference Optimization, and Proximal Policy Optimization), and that a calendar event has been created for the conference. MUST explicitly mention the conference date (April 10, 2026) and the location (San Francisco Convention Center). Keep it professional and concise (1-2 short paragraphs). Do not attach files (the file lives in a workspace the mail tool cannot reach); just reference the report by name.

DELIVERABLE: Report back (a) the calendar event ID and its confirmed start/end/location, and (b) confirmation the email was sent (recipient, subject).
